page.layout: One printed page: running text in one main column, with a narrow margin on the right holding one note. Running head at top, page number at top right, catchword and signature at the foot. The strip at the far left is the edge of the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: culè[?] fors, & servitus deploranda, cor-pora flagellis & oneribus oppressa, for-tunæ direptæ, vel diffipatæ, liberi ante oculos parentum trucidati, Duces con-tumeliis & maledictis lacessiti, Religio illusa, blasphematus Deus, & quid in-terim populus? num debacchantur in Principem, aut seditionem meditan-tur? nihil minùs: sed vires, inquies, de-fuerunt, quibus servitutis iugum excu-terent; imò, audi ipsum Pharaonem: {p}Ecce populus filiorum Israel multus, & fortior nobis est: & si defuissent vires, non potuit Moses ad præsentiam Pharaonis non semel admissus, sicam in manica gestare ad iugulum vel latus ipsius fodiendum? vel cum in Aula Re-gia viveret, venenum illi curare propi-nandum? vel denique, qui tot & tam stupenda miracula in conspectu Pharaonis operatus est, non potuit, etiam ip-sum Pharaonem si voluit miraculosè prosternere? sed noluit Deus tale ali-quod monumentum in sacris Codi-cibus posteritati traditum extare. Quid est igitur, quod tantis undique coarcta-ti angustiis moliuntur tandē? verbulo

page.notes: <note letter="p" side="right">Exod.1.9</note> Doubtful: "culè" at the start of the first line (may be "culpæ" or similar, the word is cut by the page edge). The reference mark "p" in the text is in the place where the note stands. Some italic words, such as "Moses", are uncertain in type. The short mark under "Quid" is a stroke in the print and is not transcribed.
